result.summary: Annotates CBlockIndex's nTx and m_chain_tx_count member variables with GUARDED_BY(cs_main) and enforces locking across readers. It adds cs_main locking around accesses in getchaintxstats, dumptxoutset, and blockheaderToJSON, and removes the LOCKS_EXCLUDED(cs_main) annotations from blockheader serialization helpers.
result.problem: CBlockIndex::nTx and m_chain_tx_count are updated under cs_main when block data is connected, but RPCs like getblockheader, getchaintxstats, and dumptxoutset read them without holding cs_main. This leads to data races against concurrent block receipt, pruned-node redownloads via getblockfrompeer, and AssumeUTXO background chain syncing.
evidence: PR description: 'The nTx field is modified when the block data is received and m_chain_tx_count is modified when all ancestors' block data has been received. Because of this, reading nTx from the getblockheader RPC may race as it does not acquire cs_main. Also, m_chain_tx_count may race in getchaintxstats if a pruned node redownloads a block via getblockfrompeer or if the node is running assumeutxo and tries to read m_chain_tx_count while it is being written to.'
result.changed_since_previous: No substantial changes to the approach or diff scope.
result.card: Annotates CBlockIndex fields nTx and m_chain_tx_count with GUARDED_BY(cs_main) and acquires cs_main in reader RPCs to resolve thread safety violations. Currently, getblockheader reads nTx without holding cs_main, and getchaintxstats and dumptxoutset read m_chain_tx_count without locking while those fields can be concurrently written during block receipt, pruned-node redownload, or AssumeUTXO validation. The PR removes the AssertLockNotHeld check in blockheaderToJSON and acquires cs_main during these reads.

risk.why: Introducing cs_main locking into previously lock-free RPC paths like blockheaderToJSON could introduce lock contention or deadlocks if called in unexpected lock order.
